:::{#exm-gradient-linear-approximation-quadratic}
#### A gradient that equals its linear approximation

For $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2} (x_1^2 + 3 x_2^2)$,
the [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative) is $\vecf{g} = \tp{(x_1,\ 3 x_2)}$ and the [Hessian](vector-calculus.qmd#def-hessian) is $\sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 }$ at every point (@exm-quadratic-model).
By @lem-gradient-linear-approximation,
the [linear approximation of the gradient](#def-gradient-linear-approximation) at $\vx$ is

$$
\ba
\vecf{\ell}(\stepvec)
&= \sbmat{ x_1 \\ 3 x_2 } + \sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 } \sbmat{ \step_1 \\ \step_2 }
&& \text{(@eq-gradient-linear-approximation-hessian)}
\\
&= \sbmat{ x_1 \\ 3 x_2 } + \sbmat{ \step_1 \\ 3 \step_2 }
&& \text{(matrix-vector product)}
\\
&= \sbmat{ x_1 + \step_1 \\ 3 x_2 + 3 \step_2 }
&& \text{(vector addition)}
\\
&= \sbmat{ x_1 + \step_1 \\ 3 (x_2 + \step_2) },
&& \text{(factor out } 3 \text{)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-gradient-linear-approximation-quadratic}

which is the gradient of $f$ at $\vx + \stepvec$:
the gradient of this $f$ is linear, so [its linear approximation](#def-gradient-linear-approximation) is exact.

<!-- no-figure: the approximation equals the gradient exactly, so a graph would show one surface twice -->

:::
